jobs.title: Laboratory Automation Engineer (Robotics and Digital Twins)
jobs.description:
(ID: 2026-3890)

**Axle** is a bioscience and information technology company that offers advancements in translational research, biomedical informatics, and data science applications to research centers and healthcare organizations nationally and abroad. With experts in biomedical science, software engineering, and program management, we focus on developing and applying research tools and techniques to empower decision-making and accelerate research discoveries. We work with some of the top research organizations and facilities in the country including multiple institutes at the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

  

**Benefits We Offer:**

* 100% Medical, Dental & Vision Coverage for Employees
* Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays
* 401K match up to 5%
* Educational Benefits for Career Growth
* Employee Referral Bonus
* Flexible Spending Accounts:
  + Healthcare (FSA)
  + Parking Reimbursement Account (PRK)
  + Dependent Care Assistant Program (DCAP)
  + Transportation Reimbursement Account (TRN)

**Position Overview**

  

The Laboratory Automation Engineer will program, integrate, and keep running the robots of the autonomous laboratory in Bethesda, starting with the BAB400, so that biological experiments run reliably without a person at the bench. The role builds the software layer that turns robot hardware into orchestrated, repeatable workflows, using the MADSci framework from Argonne National Laboratory. It also builds digital twins of the robots and workcells, used to plan, test, and validate protocols before they run on real hardware. The position combines hands-on robotics work in a biological lab with production-quality software development, and it works closely with IDSS data engineers, bioinformaticians, and the biologists who define the protocols.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Robot programming and control.** Program, calibrate, and maintain the BAB400 and other laboratory robots, including arms, liquid handlers, plate movers, and incubator and imaging interfaces.
* **MADSci integration.** Deploy MADSci modules, nodes, and workcell definitions so each robot and instrument can be commanded, monitored, and scheduled through a common interface. Contribute fixes and new modules back to the framework where appropriate.
* **Workflow development and scheduling.** Translate biological protocols (cell culture, iPSC maintenance, passaging, media exchange, imaging, sampling) into automated workflows with sequencing, timing, resource tracking, and recovery from failures.
* **Instrument and data integration.** Connect robot and instrument outputs to the data pipelines, LIMS, and metadata systems maintained by IDSS, so every run is logged, traceable, and reusable.
* **Validation and reliability.** Develop acceptance tests, error handling, logging, and monitoring. Troubleshoot hardware and software faults, and document root causes and fixes.
* **Safety and compliance.** Implement interlocks and safe-state behavior, and follow laboratory, biosafety, and NIH/HHS security requirements.
* **Tool evaluation.** Evaluate robots, drivers, simulators, and frameworks, and prepare short technical assessments for IDSS leadership.
* **Training and documentation.** Train laboratory staff to operate and recover the system, and write standard operating procedures and technical documentation.

  

**Required Qualifications**

The selection standard is demonstrated ability to get automated systems working. A degree in engineering, computer science, robotics, or a related science is common, but equivalent practical experience is fully acceptable.

* **Automation experience.** Several years of hands-on experience with laboratory robotics or comparable automation, such as robotic arms, liquid handlers, plate handlers, or workcells, including installing, programming, calibrating, and troubleshooting them.
* **Robot software.** Experience with the software that drives laboratory robots: vendor APIs and SDKs, device drivers, and orchestration or scheduling software.
* **Laboratory context.** Some experience with robotics in a biological laboratory (cell culture, molecular biology, or assay automation), and comfort working around biological materials under biosafety practices.
* **Programming.** Strong Python, including asynchronous or service-style code, REST APIs, and working with hardware or network protocols (serial, TCP/IP, OPC UA, or similar).
* **Software engineering practices.** Experience with Git, testing, and code review, and with Docker for deploying software next to hardware.
* **Protocol translation.** Ability to read a protocol, understand what the biology requires, and turn it into a reliable automated workflow.
* **Communication.** Strong communication skills and the ability to train laboratory staff.
* **Clearance.** Ability to obtain and maintain NIH/HHS security clearance and meet federal contractor suitability requirements.

  

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Direct experience with MADSci, or with similar laboratory orchestration frameworks (for example PyLabRobot, Opentrons tooling, or ROS-based systems).
* Experience with simulation platforms such as NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Gazebo, MoveIt, or similar robot simulators.
* Experience with stem cell, iPSC, organoid, or tissue engineering laboratories.
* Experience with self-driving or autonomous laboratories, including closed-loop experiments driven by ML or optimization.
* Familiarity with ROS 2, robot kinematics, and computer vision for labware or sample detection.
* Experience with Kubernetes, CI/CD, and message-based architectures (MQTT, Redis, or similar).
* Familiarity with LIMS, ELN, and metadata standards, and with FAIR data principles.
* Experience with imaging instruments and plate-based assays.
* Experience building or using simulation or digital-twin models of robotic systems, or a clear record of learning a new simulator quickly.

Join Stryker's Mako Robotics team and help shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery!

As an Electrical Engineer, you will take ownership of electrical designs supporting Mako's robotic end effectors, contributing to the development, integration, testing, and improvement of sophisticated medical technology.

* Experience troubleshooting electrical circuits and resolving hardware integration or system-level issues.
* Understanding of electrical system integration and interactions between hardware, software, and mechanical components.
* Experience translating engineering requirements into electrical designs, test plans, and verification activities.

* Experience supporting electromechanical systems, robotics, or other complex integrated products.

jobs.title: AI Systems Engineer, Hardware Architecture
jobs.description:
Meta Reality Labs is seeking a principal-level AI Systems Engineer to define the hardware architecture strategy for next-generation AI-accelerated computing systems powering virtual and augmented reality products. In this role, you will shape the long-term silicon and systems roadmap for on-device AI inference and training workloads across wearables, headsets, and spatial computing platforms. A core focus of this role is driving the architecture of advanced imaging systems and camera pipelines that enable real-time perception, scene understanding, and mixed reality experiences. You will drive architectural decisions that span custom silicon, memory subsystems, interconnects, image signal processors (ISPs), camera subsystems, and software-hardware co-design, ensuring Meta's AI hardware remains at the forefront of performance, efficiency, and capability for immersive computing experiences.  
  
  

### **AI Systems Engineer, Hardware Architecture Responsibilities:**

* Define multi-generation hardware architecture strategy for AI inference and training systems across VR, AR, and wearable device platforms
* Lead system-level architectural exploration and trade-off analysis across compute, memory hierarchy, interconnect fabric, and power delivery for on-device AI workloads
* Architect end-to-end camera and imaging pipelines, including sensor interfaces, ISP integration, and real-time image processing for computer vision and perception applications
* Drive hardware-software co-design initiatives by partnering with silicon engineering, firmware, camera systems, and ML platform teams to optimize end-to-end AI and imaging pipeline performance
* Define architectural requirements for camera subsystems including multi-camera synchronization, depth sensing, and low-latency visual processing for AR/VR applications
* Establish architectural requirements and performance targets for custom AI accelerators, ISPs, SoCs, and supporting subsystems in spatial computing devices
* Develop and maintain system performance models and simulation frameworks to evaluate architectural decisions against real-world AI and imaging workload characteristics
* Provide architectural guidance and technical direction across hardware engineering organizations, aligning imaging and AI roadmaps with product and research priorities
* Identify and resolve system-level bottlenecks in imaging latency, AI inference throughput, and energy efficiency for wearable and headset form factors
* Engage with external silicon partners, camera module vendors, and research institutions to evaluate emerging imaging technologies and incorporate them into long-range architecture plans
* Communicate architectural vision and technical rationale to executive leadership and cross-functional stakeholders through written proposals and design reviews

  
  
  

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* 12+ years of experience in hardware systems architecture, with a focus on AI, ML, imaging systems, or high-performance compute systems
* Deep expertise in camera pipeline architecture, including image signal processing (ISP), sensor integration, and end-to-end imaging system design
* Experience defining SoC or system-level architecture for AI inference or training workloads, including memory subsystem design, compute hierarchy, and interconnect topology
* Experience architecting imaging subsystems for real-time computer vision applications, including multi-camera systems, depth sensing, and visual-inertial odometry
* Experience developing system performance models and using simulation or analytical frameworks to evaluate architectural trade-offs at scale
* Track record of driving multi-year hardware architecture roadmaps for imaging and AI systems and influencing silicon strategy across large engineering organizations

  
  
  

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Familiarity with custom silicon development flows for imaging and AI accelerators, including architecture-to-RTL handoff, physical design constraints, and post-silicon validation
* Experience architecting AI and imaging systems for power- and area-constrained wearable or mobile devices, including VR headsets, AR glasses, or similar spatial computing platforms
* Expertise in computational photography pipelines, HDR processing, and neural ISP architectures
* Background in collaborating with ML research and camera teams to translate novel imaging algorithms and model architectures into hardware-efficient deployment targets
* Experience evaluating and integrating emerging memory technologies (e.g., HBM, LPDDR5X, in-memory compute) into AI and imaging system architectures

  
  
  

### **About Meta:**

Meta builds technologies that help people connect, find communities, and grow businesses. When Facebook launched in 2004, it changed the way people connect. Apps like Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp further empowered billions around the world. Now, Meta is moving beyond 2D screens toward immersive experiences like augmented and virtual reality to help build the next evolution in social technology. People who choose to build their careers by building with us at Meta help shape a future that will take us beyond what digital connection makes possible today—beyond the constraints of screens, the limits of distance, and even the rules of physics.  
  
  

Meta is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. R2 is growing rapidly, and the metadata layer must evolve to keep pace. You'll be joining a team that operates at the intersection of distributed databases, large scale storage infrastructure, and edge computing; building systems that need to be correct, fast, and reliable.

* Own the schema, data model, and query patterns for a metadata layer managing billions of objects across multiple distributed database clusters.
* Own projects end to end; from design docs and schema changes through implementation, testing, deployment, and production monitoring.
* Participate in oncall rotations, drive incident resolution, and write postmortems that improve reliability.
* Use AI tools extensively to accelerate development, debugging, and operational tasks. We expect engineers to leverage AI as a core part of their workflow.

You should be comfortable using AI-native tools, agents, harnesses, and automation to improve your own engineering loop — and interested in building the internal tools and context that help a small team ship like a much larger one.

### **Responsibilities**

* Build core AI Gateway systems that handle high-volume inference traffic across providers, models, and Cloudflare's global network.
* Design and implement APIs, routing primitives, observability features, controls, and developer workflows that make AI Gateway reliable and easy to adopt.
* Work across product and infrastructure boundaries with Workers AI, Agents, and the broader Developer Platform organization to make Cloudflare's AI platform feel like one coherent product.
* Turn ambiguous product and technical ideas into prototypes, design docs, shipped features, and measurable production improvements.
* Improve reliability, performance, cost efficiency, and debuggability for latency-sensitive AI workloads.
* Build the software — and the software that builds the software: agents, tests, harnesses, evaluation loops, operational tools, and internal context that help the team move faster with confidence.

### **Desirable Skills, Knowledge & Experience**

* 5+ years of experience building and operating production systems, ideally in AI infrastructure, developer platforms, cloud infrastructure, edge/proxy systems, high-scale APIs, or distributed systems.
* Strong systems engineering fundamentals: networking, APIs, reliability, observability, data modeling, performance, and operational tradeoffs.
* Experience designing or scaling distributed systems where latency, throughput, availability, and correctness all matter.
* Ability to work comfortably across the stack, from API design and product surfaces to backend services, queues, storage systems, control planes, or performance-critical code.
* Strong developer tools taste. You have used and built enough APIs, SDKs, dashboards, CLIs, docs, and internal platforms to know what makes them delightful or painful.

* A builder's bias toward working software. You can prototype quickly, ship incrementally, and improve systems while they are already in production.
* Operational judgment. You understand that at Cloudflare scale, rare bugs are not rare for long, and you build systems that are observable, resilient, and recoverable.

jobs.title: Software Engineering Manager, AI Kernels & Performance Optimization — MTIA Software
jobs.description:
Meta designs and deploys its own AI systems. MTIA — the Meta Training and Inference Accelerator — is Meta's family of in-house AI accelerator ASICs, running recommendation and ranking workloads in production across Meta's data centers today and expanding into generative AI inference and training as successive silicon generations land.The MTIA Software team is part of the AI & Compute Foundation (ACF) organization within Meta Infrastructure. We build the entire stack a chip vendor would normally supply — compiler and LLVM toolchain, runtime, kernel authoring frameworks and libraries, developer tooling, and deep PyTorch integration — co-designing it with the silicon teams generation over generation.Within that stack, the AI Kernels and Performance Optimization team (KORE) owns the layer where silicon architecture meets arithmetic. Our mission is roofline-level performance and programmability at scale: we design and implement high-performance compute and communication kernels (GEMM, attention variants, normalization, collectives, elementwise and reduction fusions, sparse and quantized paths) against novel architectural features including matrix engines, on-chip reduction fabrics, and software-managed memory hierarchies. We ship kernel libraries with broad PyTorch operator coverage, build C++ and Python kernel authoring frameworks and DSL surfaces, and write production kernels against new architectures long before first silicon — turning hardware proposals into measured roofline evidence while the design can still change.We are seeking a Software Engineering Manager to lead a team of kernel and performance engineers doing this work. You will own the performance of workloads that serve billions of people, drive technical strategy for kernel development and optimization, and build a team that can deliver roofline-level performance on MTIA accelerators. Your team will profile and root-cause performance across the full stack — instruction scheduling, memory hierarchy and DMA behavior, on-chip interconnect, multi-device collectives — and drive fixes to the right layer, whether that is the kernel, compiler, runtime, or hardware. You will partner closely with silicon architecture teams on hardware/software co-design, quantifying the value of proposed features with real kernels and advocating for the changes the software stack needs. This is a hands-on technical leadership role where you will contribute directly to architectural decisions while enabling your team to move with speed and clarity.  
  
  

### **Software Engineering Manager, AI Kernels & Performance Optimization — MTIA Software Responsibilities:**

* Lead and manage a team of systems engineers delivering on multiple concurrent projects across ambiguous, high-impact areas of Meta's platform infrastructure
* Drive roadmap creation and technical strategy for systems-level software, ensuring alignment with broader product and engineering goals
* Contribute directly to technical work including architecture reviews, design documents, and hands-on coding to maintain credibility and unblock the team
* Identify and resolve systemic issues affecting team velocity, including on-call load, technical debt, and gaps in tooling or automation
* Partner with product, design, and data science to ensure engineers contribute across disciplines and deliver outcomes that move business metrics forward
* Set clear goals and expectations for individual engineers, provide timely and actionable feedback, and proactively address performance gaps
* Manage staged rollouts and feature delivery using feature flagging and A/B testing frameworks, ensuring high engineering quality and system reliability
* Recruit, onboard, and develop engineers, building a team structure that minimizes single points of failure and scales with organizational needs
* Communicate team goals, technical decisions, and progress clearly to cross-functional partners and leadership, including written design proposals and postmortems
* Participate in org-wide engineering contributions, sharing effective workflows, tooling practices, and systems engineering patterns across the broader organization

  
  
  

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* 4+ years of experience in software engineering with a focus on systems-level software, platform infrastructure, or distributed systems
* 2+ years of experience managing or leading engineering teams, including setting technical direction and supporting engineer growth
* Experience driving technical roadmaps and executing against them with measurable outcomes in ambiguous or high-complexity environments
* Experience identifying and resolving engineering efficiency issues such as on-call burden, technical debt, or gaps in automation
* Experience collaborating across product, design, and data functions to deliver software that achieves business and user impact

  
  
  

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Track record of hands-on technical contribution as a manager, including authoring design documents, reviewing system architectures, or writing production code
* Experience with hardware/software co-design cycles: collaborating with silicon architects, validating architectural features with real kernels, and influencing hardware roadmaps based on software performance analysis
* Experience working on customized AI accelerators (TPU, AI ASICs, or similar non-GPU architectures) with direct involvement in kernel development and roofline enablement
* Familiarity with transformer and attention kernel design: FlashAttention-class algorithms, KV-cache management, paged and chunked attention, MoE routing and expert dispatch
* Experience with distributed execution and collective communication (NCCL/RCCL-class primitives, tensor and expert parallelism, overlapping communication with compute)
* Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies

jobs.title: Senior Firmware & System Debug Engineer
jobs.description:
**Overview**

Microsoft Silicon and Cloud Hardware Infrastructure Engineering (SCHIE) is the team behind Microsoft’s expanding Cloud Infrastructure and responsible for powering Microsoft’s “Intelligent Cloud” mission. SCHIE delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's over 200 online businesses including Bing, MSN, Office 365, Xbox Live, Skype, OneDrive and the Microsoft Azure platform globally with our server and data center infrastructure, security and compliance, operations, globalization, and manageability solutions.

We in SCHIE’s Firmware Center of Excellence create the foundational firmware that powers the Microsoft Cloud. Our firmware lights up millions of servers and racks across the globe, enabling users to do everything from running blogs to crunching through powerful AI algorithms. We’re a growing team of diverse, talented & passionate engineers inventing and delivering technology to light up the “world’s computer!” We are working on the next generation hardware/firmware for server, silicon and rack infrastructure with a focus on innovation in firmware technology to secure Azure infrastructure for Microsoft and their customers. We believe that a robust firmware infrastructure leads to incredibly powerful computing experiences—if you believe this too, we need you!

Microsoft's first-party (1P) Firmware team is seeking a **Senior Firmware & System Debug Engineer** for future MAIA and Cobalt products from silicon bring-up through production fleet operation. You will lead embedded firmware development, investigations across firmware, silicon, hardware, operating systems, and drivers; develop debug capabilities and telemetry-analysis capabilities; and apply automation, data science, and AI-assisted tools to accelerate root-cause analysis at scale. We are looking for someone with demonstated experience with firmware development, debug, technical investigations and identifying fixes.

#azurehwjobs #SCHIE

  
  
**Responsibilities**  

* Lead embedded firmware development, debug and fixes for silicon/SOC issues.
* Own complex investigations into firmware crashes, boot/reset failures, hangs, memory corruption, and hardware/software interaction issues across MAIA and Cobalt.
* Correlate firmware logs, silicon error records, crash dumps, OS/driver traces, configuration, and fleet telemetry to isolate failure mechanisms.
* Develop reproducible experiments and targeted diagnostic firmware or tooling to test hypotheses and distinguish firmware defects from silicon, hardware, or software causes.
* Build scalable analysis and triage automation, including failure bucketing, signature detection, cohort comparisons, and regression detection.
* Apply statistical analysis and AI-assisted methods to prioritize investigations and reduce manual analysis, validating results against independent evidence.
* Drive mitigations and permanent fixes with component owners; verify effectiveness through regression testing and post-deployment telemetry.
* Convert investigation findings into improved instrumentation, test coverage, troubleshooting guidance, and mentoring

**Required Qualifications:**

* Experience with cross-layer root-cause analysis of firmware, silicon, or system failures using logs, crash dumps, or telemetry.
* Experience reading and debugging C/C++ firmware, together with scripting experience for automation or engineering-data analysis.

jobs.description:
**Locations and Workstyle:**

**Blue Bell, PA**: Primarily remote; candidates should be within commuting distance of the Blue Bell office and able to work onsite as needed. Option to come onsite more frequently if desired.
  
**Irving, TX** and **Boca Raton, FL**: Hybrid schedule – onsite a minimum of four days per week, with one remote day. Five days onsite may be required based on business needs.

**What you should know about our team:**
  
You’ll join a Product Engineering environment focused on developing reliable embedded software for security systems. In this role, you’ll work hands-on across embedded Linux development, system integration, build and release automation, and production support. You’ll collaborate closely with Systems, Hardware, Quality, DevOps, Security, and Product teams to turn requirements into production-ready software.

**What you will do:**

* You’ll own meaningful pieces of the embedded software lifecycle, from design and development through testing, integration, and release. Your work will help improve the reliability, repeatability, and quality of the software and firmware that powers our security products.
* Design, develop, debug, test, and maintain C/C++ software and firmware in embedded Linux environments.
* Build and enhance Linux platform components, including system services, device interfaces, networking functions, board configurations, and hardware and cloud integrations.
* Deliver maintainable, production-quality code and unit tests while reviewing pull requests and ensuring changes meet architecture, security, quality, and coding standards.
* Own and improve embedded build and release environments using Buildroot, cross-compilation toolchains, package integration, versioning, system image generation, and artifact management.
* Automate and maintain build, test, and release pipelines incorporating continuous integration, static analysis, test execution, release validation, and deployment readiness.
* Investigate and resolve build, integration, and release failures through root-cause analysis and corrective actions that improve reliability and release quality.
* Integrate and govern AI-assisted engineering tools for development, code review, test generation, defect analysis, and documentation while applying appropriate validation, security, IP, and traceability controls.
* Collaborate across Systems, Hardware, Quality, DevOps, Security, and Product teams while developing reusable automation, frameworks, and engineering practices.

**What you need to be successful:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Management Information Systems, or equivalent experience.
* Strong hands-on experience developing and debugging C/C++ software in embedded Linux environments.
* Knowledge of Linux kernel concepts, device interfaces, system services, networking, and software security.
* Hands-on experience with Buildroot, including configuration, package integration, board configuration, cross-compilation, system image generation, and build troubleshooting.
* Experience supporting firmware release processes, including firmware over-the-air releases.
* Experience managing automated build, test, and release pipelines for embedded products.

* Experience with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, LTE, Z-Wave, Matter, or Thread.

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

We are looking for a Firmware Engineer with a strong background in low level firmware and SoC power management.

As part of the Power Management Firmware (PMFW) team, the Engineer will design, develop, integrate, and debug firmware responsible for power management and platform control across AMD SoCs. The role spans pre silicon development and validation through silicon bring up, production readiness, and customer enablement.

The engineer will work closely with firmware architects, silicon design, power and performance teams, BIOS, validation, and other firmware teams to develop robust platform firmware and drive complex issues to resolution.

* Participate in peer reviews, identify, track and repair defects

Prescient Edge is seeking a **Electrical Engineer - Controls & Automation** to support a Federal Government client.

* Perform power-load calculations and support management of system electrical budgets.

jobs.title: Software Engineering Manager, AI Kernels & Performance Optimization — MTIA Software
jobs.description:
Meta designs and deploys its own AI systems. MTIA — the Meta Training and Inference Accelerator — is Meta's family of in-house AI accelerator ASICs, running recommendation and ranking workloads in production across Meta's data centers today and expanding into generative AI inference and training as successive silicon generations land.The MTIA Software team is part of the AI & Compute Foundation (ACF) organization within Meta Infrastructure. We build the entire stack a chip vendor would normally supply — compiler and LLVM toolchain, runtime, kernel authoring frameworks and libraries, developer tooling, and deep PyTorch integration — co-designing it with the silicon teams generation over generation.Within that stack, the AI Kernels and Performance Optimization team (KORE) owns the layer where silicon architecture meets arithmetic. Our mission is roofline-level performance and programmability at scale: we design and implement high-performance compute and communication kernels (GEMM, attention variants, normalization, collectives, elementwise and reduction fusions, sparse and quantized paths) against novel architectural features including matrix engines, on-chip reduction fabrics, and software-managed memory hierarchies. We ship kernel libraries with broad PyTorch operator coverage, build C++ and Python kernel authoring frameworks and DSL surfaces, and write production kernels against new architectures long before first silicon — turning hardware proposals into measured roofline evidence while the design can still change.We are seeking a Software Engineering Manager to lead a team of kernel and performance engineers doing this work. You will own the performance of workloads that serve billions of people, drive technical strategy for kernel development and optimization, and build a team that can deliver roofline-level performance on MTIA accelerators. Your team will profile and root-cause performance across the full stack — instruction scheduling, memory hierarchy and DMA behavior, on-chip interconnect, multi-device collectives — and drive fixes to the right layer, whether that is the kernel, compiler, runtime, or hardware. You will partner closely with silicon architecture teams on hardware/software co-design, quantifying the value of proposed features with real kernels and advocating for the changes the software stack needs. This is a hands-on technical leadership role where you will contribute directly to architectural decisions while enabling your team to move with speed and clarity.

* Lead and manage a team of systems engineers delivering on multiple concurrent projects across ambiguous, high-impact areas of Meta's platform infrastructure
* Drive roadmap creation and technical strategy for systems-level software, ensuring alignment with broader product and engineering goals
* Contribute directly to technical work including architecture reviews, design documents, and hands-on coding to maintain credibility and unblock the team
* Identify and resolve systemic issues affecting team velocity, including on-call load, technical debt, and gaps in tooling or automation

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* 4+ years of experience in software engineering with a focus on systems-level software, platform infrastructure, or distributed systems
* 2+ years of experience managing or leading engineering teams, including setting technical direction and supporting engineer growth
* Experience driving technical roadmaps and executing against them with measurable outcomes in ambiguous or high-complexity environments
* Experience identifying and resolving engineering efficiency issues such as on-call burden, technical debt, or gaps in automation
* Experience collaborating across product, design, and data functions to deliver software that achieves business and user impact

* Experience with hardware/software co-design cycles: collaborating with silicon architects, validating architectural features with real kernels, and influencing hardware roadmaps based on software performance analysis
* Experience working on customized AI accelerators (TPU, AI ASICs, or similar non-GPU architectures) with direct involvement in kernel development and roofline enablement

new_jobs.title: Embedded Systems Engineer, Robotics
new_jobs.description:
**ABOUT DEXMATE**

Dexmate is building the foundation for physical AI — combining a new generation of robots with a universal Physical AI OS, making robots as easy to build and deploy as software. Today, robotics is fragmented, slow, and closed: most builders are forced to reinvent the same stack again and again, and most ideas never make it past the prototype stage. We exist to change that. Our mission is to democratize robotics by lowering the barrier to entry, delivering a plug-and-play platform for developers, researchers, and enterprises, and cultivating an open ecosystem that accelerates the evolution of physical AI.

If you want to help shape the next layer of human capability — and believe the future of robotics should be built together, not in isolation — we'd love to build it with you.

**THE ROLE**

We're looking for an Embedded Systems Engineer to own the boundary where our robot's electronics meet its software. You will bring up and debug new PCBs, write the firmware and drivers that make every sensor, camera, actuator, and compute module talk to each other, and make sure data moves reliably across CAN/CAN FD, EtherCAT, GMSL, I2C, SPI, and Ethernet.

This is a hands-on, cross-layer role. One day you're probing a board with a scope to find why a bus is dropping frames; the next you're writing a Linux driver for a camera serializer or tuning an EtherCAT network for deterministic timing. You'll work closely with electrical, firmware, controls, and robotics software engineers, and you'll often be the person who figures out whether a problem lives in hardware, firmware, or software.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Bringing up, validating, and debugging new PCBs: reading schematics and layouts, measuring signals, and isolating hardware vs. software faults
* Developing firmware for MCUs (bare-metal and RTOS) and drivers for embedded Linux platforms (e.g., NVIDIA Jetson / Orin)
* Writing and maintaining device drivers and communication stacks for CAN/CAN FD, EtherCAT, I2C, SPI, UART, and Ethernet
* Integrating camera and sensor pipelines over GMSL (serializer/deserializer configuration, device trees, V4L2 drivers, timing and synchronization)
* Bringing up and tuning EtherCAT and CAN networks across actuators, sensors, and power systems for deterministic, real-time performance
* Debugging signal-integrity, power, timing, and bus-level issues with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and protocol analyzers
* Contributing firmware and software input during schematic and PCB design reviews to make boards easier to bring up, test, and debug
* Building diagnostics, test fixtures, and automated hardware-in-the-loop tests for boards and subsystems
* Supporting manufacturing, end-of-line testing, and field troubleshooting as robots move from prototype to deployment
* Documenting interfaces, bring-up procedures, and debugging playbooks for the wider team

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

* 3+ years of professional experience in embedded systems in robotics, automotive, industrial automation, or complex consumer electronics
* Strong C and C++ skills for firmware and driver development; working knowledge of Python for tooling and test automation
* Hands-on board bring-up experience, including reading schematics, PCB layouts, datasheets, and timing diagrams
* Driver-level experience with several of: CAN/CAN FD, EtherCAT, I2C, SPI, UART, Ethernet
* Experience with MCU firmware (ARM Cortex-M, STM32, TI C2000, or similar) on bare-metal or RTOS platforms
* Comfort with embedded debugging and lab tools: JTAG/SWD debuggers, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and protocol analyzers
* Systematic debugging skills across the hardware, firmware, and software boundary
* Strong communication skills and comfort working directly with electrical, mechanical, controls, and software engineers

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Experience with GMSL or other high-speed camera links (e.g., MAX9295/MAX9296, FPD-Link), MIPI CSI-2, and V4L2
* Embedded Linux kernel and device-driver development, device trees, and BSP bring-up (NVIDIA Jetson / Orin a plus)
* Experience integrating EtherCAT master or slave stacks (SOEM, IgH, or equivalent)

Cloudflare's Developer Platform powers stateful, data-intensive applications across our network. We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to work across the database stack, from query planning and execution to transaction processing and durable storage.

You'll make decisions that shape the consistency, durability, and latency guarantees that customer applications rely on.

Correctness under concurrency and failure is central to the role. You'll define and implement how queries read and modify data, how concurrent transactions become visible, and how durable state is recovered. You'll validate these systems using deterministic simulation, workload testing, and evidence from production.

### **Responsibilities**

* Improve query planning and execution, including index selection, row reads and writes, and performance as data volumes and access patterns change.
* Build transaction and storage paths that make writes durable and reads consistent. Define when changes become visible, how commits survive failure, and how recovery restores a correct view of the data.
* Design deterministic simulations that make rare event orderings and failures reproducible.
* Plan stateful upgrades that cannot be reversed by rolling back software. Carry them through staged rollout, failover, and recovery without putting existing data at risk.
* Participate in the service's on-call rotation and incident response.
* Own major changes from design through production. Coordinate implementation across teams when a change spans multiple parts of the service, and help trace failures across those parts.
* Mentor other engineers through design reviews, debugging, and incident analysis involving concurrency, durability, and recovery.

### **Desirable Skills, Knowledge & Experience**

* You have owned a database, storage engine, transaction system, or similarly correctness-sensitive stateful system from architecture through production. You can make architecture and implementation decisions when requirements or system boundaries are incomplete.
* You understand how query execution, indexing, transaction processing, and durable state shape what developers and operators observe.
* You understand how concurrency control, isolation, replication, and snapshots shape consistency, durability, and recovery. You can apply those concepts when operations arrive out of order, components fail independently, or the network partitions.
* You write and debug concurrent production software in Rust, Go, C++, or another systems language. You can trace failures across process, network, and durable-state boundaries.
* You have operated stateful systems through rollouts, scaling events, incidents, and recovery. You know the difference between transient unavailability and incomplete or incorrect recovery, and when a system is safe to return to service.
* You have led investigations where failures crossed systems owned by several teams.

### **Bonus Points**

* You've worked on the internals of PostgreSQL, MySQL, Amazon Aurora, or another relational database and can trace a SQL operation from planning through commit.
* Your work on transaction processing or concurrency control has included defining snapshot visibility and recovery behavior.
* You've profiled database workloads and traced performance bottlenecks from query execution through durable storage.
* You've used deterministic simulation or another systematic method to uncover distributed-systems bugs that conventional tests missed.

new_jobs.title: Software Engineering Manager, AI Kernels & Performance Optimization — MTIA Software
new_jobs.description:
Meta designs and deploys its own AI systems. MTIA — the Meta Training and Inference Accelerator — is Meta's family of in-house AI accelerator ASICs, running recommendation and ranking workloads in production across Meta's data centers today and expanding into generative AI inference and training as successive silicon generations land.The MTIA Software team is part of the AI & Compute Foundation (ACF) organization within Meta Infrastructure. We build the entire stack a chip vendor would normally supply — compiler and LLVM toolchain, runtime, kernel authoring frameworks and libraries, developer tooling, and deep PyTorch integration — co-designing it with the silicon teams generation over generation.Within that stack, the AI Kernels and Performance Optimization team (KORE) owns the layer where silicon architecture meets arithmetic. Our mission is roofline-level performance and programmability at scale: we design and implement high-performance compute and communication kernels (GEMM, attention variants, normalization, collectives, elementwise and reduction fusions, sparse and quantized paths) against novel architectural features including matrix engines, on-chip reduction fabrics, and software-managed memory hierarchies. We ship kernel libraries with broad PyTorch operator coverage, build C++ and Python kernel authoring frameworks and DSL surfaces, and write production kernels against new architectures long before first silicon — turning hardware proposals into measured roofline evidence while the design can still change.We are seeking a Software Engineering Manager to lead a team of kernel and performance engineers doing this work. You will own the performance of workloads that serve billions of people, drive technical strategy for kernel development and optimization, and build a team that can deliver roofline-level performance on MTIA accelerators. Your team will profile and root-cause performance across the full stack — instruction scheduling, memory hierarchy and DMA behavior, on-chip interconnect, multi-device collectives — and drive fixes to the right layer, whether that is the kernel, compiler, runtime, or hardware. You will partner closely with silicon architecture teams on hardware/software co-design, quantifying the value of proposed features with real kernels and advocating for the changes the software stack needs. This is a hands-on technical leadership role where you will contribute directly to architectural decisions while enabling your team to move with speed and clarity.  
  
  

### **Software Engineering Manager, AI Kernels & Performance Optimization — MTIA Software Responsibilities:**

* Lead and manage a team of systems engineers delivering on multiple concurrent projects across ambiguous, high-impact areas of Meta's platform infrastructure
* Drive roadmap creation and technical strategy for systems-level software, ensuring alignment with broader product and engineering goals
* Contribute directly to technical work including architecture reviews, design documents, and hands-on coding to maintain credibility and unblock the team
* Identify and resolve systemic issues affecting team velocity, including on-call load, technical debt, and gaps in tooling or automation
* Partner with product, design, and data science to ensure engineers contribute across disciplines and deliver outcomes that move business metrics forward
* Set clear goals and expectations for individual engineers, provide timely and actionable feedback, and proactively address performance gaps
* Manage staged rollouts and feature delivery using feature flagging and A/B testing frameworks, ensuring high engineering quality and system reliability
* Recruit, onboard, and develop engineers, building a team structure that minimizes single points of failure and scales with organizational needs
* Communicate team goals, technical decisions, and progress clearly to cross-functional partners and leadership, including written design proposals and postmortems
* Participate in org-wide engineering contributions, sharing effective workflows, tooling practices, and systems engineering patterns across the broader organization

  
  
  

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* 4+ years of experience in software engineering with a focus on systems-level software, platform infrastructure, or distributed systems
* 2+ years of experience managing or leading engineering teams, including setting technical direction and supporting engineer growth
* Experience driving technical roadmaps and executing against them with measurable outcomes in ambiguous or high-complexity environments
* Experience identifying and resolving engineering efficiency issues such as on-call burden, technical debt, or gaps in automation
* Experience collaborating across product, design, and data functions to deliver software that achieves business and user impact

  
  
  

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Track record of hands-on technical contribution as a manager, including authoring design documents, reviewing system architectures, or writing production code
* Experience with hardware/software co-design cycles: collaborating with silicon architects, validating architectural features with real kernels, and influencing hardware roadmaps based on software performance analysis
* Experience working on customized AI accelerators (TPU, AI ASICs, or similar non-GPU architectures) with direct involvement in kernel development and roofline enablement
* Familiarity with transformer and attention kernel design: FlashAttention-class algorithms, KV-cache management, paged and chunked attention, MoE routing and expert dispatch
* Experience with distributed execution and collective communication (NCCL/RCCL-class primitives, tensor and expert parallelism, overlapping communication with compute)
* Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
* Experience managing or leading

new_jobs.title: Senior Spacecraft Systems Engineer, Avionics
new_jobs.description:
**About Varda**
---------------

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. **Varda's W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.**

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

**About This Role**
-------------------

The **Senior Spacecraft Systems Engineer, Avionics** oversees the design, integration, and testing of avionics systems for our Winnebago Spaceship. They ensure that all systems are ready for both launch and operational phases, requiring a deep understanding of avionics system design, manufacturing processes, and operational protocols. They closely collaborate with various engineering teams and navigate conflicting requirements to achieve seamless system integration. Their expertise will be crucial in ensuring the vehicle meets its mission objectives, from space manufacturing to hypersonic testing during reentry.

### **Responsibilities**

* Collaborate with cross functional teams to define project scopes and initial requirements, guiding designs from concept to prototype and full-scale production.
* Develop electrical architecture, system diagrams, and budgets to account for power, telemetry, channel count, size, and mass predictions used to communicate closing vehicle solutions to company level objectives.
* Analyze architecture for potential faults and risks, develop comprehensive mitigation plans, resolve uncertainties, and collaborate on Fault Detection Isolation and Recovery (FDIR) or operational workarounds when hardware solutions are unfeasible.
* Conduct comprehensive verification plans for avionics systems on flight and HITL hardware, ensuring readiness for launch and compliance with mission objectives for space and reentry operations.
* Participate in mission operations as an Avionics specialist or system operator, where they'll determine system health, suggest corrective actions to reentry commit criteria for operational success.
* Oversee the integration of the Winnebago avionics systems, acting as the primary point of contact for integrated systems investigations.
* Design, build, and operate the Hardware In The Loop (HITL) testbeds, simulating the spacecraft on the ground to ensure all systems are mission ready.
* Develop avionics ground infrastructure, support the design and integration of test racks and R&D equipment used to power and communicate with the flight vehicles. Contribute to developing engineering best practices, focusing on increased test automation and efficiency.
* Draw from their experiences to help mentor and train new engineers, fostering a culture of learning and continuous improvement within the team.

### **Basic Qualifications**

* Education: Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical field.
* Experience: 5+ years of experience in system design, test planning, and validation.
* Programming Skills: Proficiency in programming and debugging with Python.
* Technical Expertise: Experience with power supplies, modular DAQ systems, RTD and 4-20mA devices, and general test equipment.

### **Preferred Skills and Experience**

* Proven experience taking vehicle electrical systems from concept to operational production.
* Prior experience setting up HITL testbeds, managing configuration control, and conducting system level tests.
* Familiarity with Unix environments and the ability to use command line utilities.
* Experience developing test cases and test equipment to meet vehicle operating conditions.
* Strong project or program management skills.
* Relevant prior roles: Avionics Hardware, FPGA Engineer, Electronics Test Engineer, Electrical Systems Engineer

### **Pay Range**

* Salary range: Senior: $140,333 - $202,703/ per year
* This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA
* Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance
* You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

**ITAR Requirements**
---------------------

Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire "U.S. persons" who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.  
  
"US person" means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).

  

**E-Verify Statement**
----------------------

Varda Spac

new_jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. The Reliability & Maintenance Engineering (RME) team are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it happen. We drive continuous improvement, and maintain all the robotics and material handling equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey!  
  
About the Role:  
As a Senior Automation Engineer, you will play a crucial role in maximizing equipment reliability and operational performance in our fulfillment centers by providing proactive controls automation and technical support. Your expertise will be essential in troubleshooting complex control systems, analyzing performance metrics, and driving continuous improvement initiatives. You'll mentor junior engineers and lead cross-functional teams to optimize material handling equipment (MHE) systems, implement innovative projects, and develop system design improvements to enhance site throughput. You'll work with state-of-the-art technology, including conveyors, sortation systems, scanners, cameras, print and apply systems, and SCADA devices and programs. Through your technical leadership and design optimization efforts, you'll directly contribute to ensuring our customers receive their orders with Amazon's signature speed and accuracy while building team capabilities and driving operational excellence.  
  
What Do We Offer?  
Amazon offers competitive compensation packages including comprehensive healthcare benefits starting on Day 1, matching 401(k) program, and up to 20 weeks of paid parental leave. But wait, there’s more: We provide lightweight fire-resistant daily wear and composite toe safety shoes for your safety!  
  
Key job responsibilities  
Key job responsibilities include, but are not limited to:  

* You will apply Subject Matter Expertise (SME) on troubleshooting and dive deeps for engineering issues, supporting automation engineers to investigate the root cause and planning actions to eliminate/mitigate the downtime of critical assets
* You will collaborate with building Operations, Operations Engineering teams, FC Start-up Team, AFT Software teams, ACES team, and Safety to support MHE systems optimization and project implementation
* You will understand, maintain and troubleshoot material handling control systems, including PLC/PC controllers and industrial networks such as Ethernet, ControlNet, DeviceNet, Profibus, motor control systems, servo drives, frequency drives, and electrical distribution systems
* You will monitor MHE metrics and partner with maintenance/operations to address system performance issues and provide analysis across all operations
* You will provide escalation support to automation engineers, during and after business hours, troubleshooting locally and remotely, to ensure that all hardware or controls software within the building is repaired on time
* You must be able to move up to 49lbs, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, climb ladders and gangways safely and without limitation, as well as perform regular bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching both below the waist and above the head

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, automation engineering, or equivalent, or 4+ years of PLC programming or automation engineering experience
* Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
* 4+ years of process or production environment related PLC-controlled automation and issue diagnosis experience
* 4+ years of robotics work cells and control systems experience
* 4+ years of Siemens, Allen-Bradley or Codesys Ladder Logic and structure programming experience
* 4+ years of electrical theory, robotics, controls components, and automated equipment experience

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* Master's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, automation engineering, or equivalent
* Master's degree, or Six Sigma Black Belt certification
* Experience leading controls in manufacturing or complex industrial environments
* Experience identifying, maintaining, troubleshooting, and modifying Motor Controls including motor starters, Variable Frequency Drives, DC drives, and standard electrical components
* Experience interpreting and modifying mechanical and electrical drawings

**Job Description**

**The Role**

The Manufacturing Automation Engineer – Cobots leads the development, deployment, optimization, and sustainment of manufacturing automation solutions across GPS manufacturing sites. This role combines deep manufacturing engineering expertise with end-to-end project leadership.

  

You will identify processes suitable for automation, evaluate the right solution—including collaborative robots (cobots), traditional industrial robots, vision systems, controls, and other automation technologies—and lead turnkey projects from concept through launch and sustainment. You will partner with plant teams, manufacturing engineering, controls and automation teams, suppliers, and business stakeholders to deliver solutions that improve safety, quality, ergonomics, throughput, labor efficiency, equipment utilization, and cost performance.

  

This role supports projects across multiple plant locations. Travel is expected to vary by project phase and may reach 50% or more, including overnight travel and extended time at manufacturing plants during equipment build, installation, commissioning, and launch. Travel may exceed 50% during critical launch periods.

  

**What You’ll Do**

* Visit manufacturing plants and assess current processes, production requirements, and operational constraints.
* Identify and prioritize automation opportunities that improve safety, ergonomics, quality, cycle time, labor efficiency, uptime, and cost.
* Conduct feasibility studies and determine the appropriate solution, including cobots, traditional industrial robots, vision systems, controls, tooling, sensors, and related technologies.
* Lead turnkey automation projects from concept and planning through design, equipment build, installation, commissioning, validation, launch, sustainment, and closeout.
* Develop project scopes, Statements of Requirements (SORs), technical specifications, project plans, timing, deliverables, and risk and issue-management plans.

### **About the Role**

Cloudflare's Developer Platform powers stateful, data-intensive applications across our network. We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to work across the database stack, from query planning and execution to transaction processing and durable storage.

You'll make decisions that shape the consistency, durability, and latency guarantees that customer applications rely on.

Correctness under concurrency and failure is central to the role. You'll define and implement how queries read and modify data, how concurrent transactions become visible, and how durable state is recovered. You'll validate these systems using deterministic simulation, workload testing, and evidence from production.

### **Responsibilities**

* Improve query planning and execution, including index selection, row reads and writes, and performance as data volumes and access patterns change.
* Build transaction and storage paths that make writes durable and reads consistent. Define when changes become visible, how commits survive failure, and how recovery restores a correct view of the data.
* Design deterministic simulations that make rare event orderings and failures reproducible.
* Plan stateful upgrades that cannot be reversed by rolling back software. Carry them through staged rollout, failover, and recovery without putting existing data at risk.
* Participate in the service's on-call rotation and incident response.
* Own major changes from design through production. Coordinate implementation across teams when a change spans multiple parts of the service, and help trace failures across those parts.
* Mentor other engineers through design reviews, debugging, and incident analysis involving concurrency, durability, and recovery.

### **Desirable Skills, Knowledge & Experience**

* You have owned a database, storage engine, transaction system, or similarly correctness-sensitive stateful system from architecture through production. You can make architecture and implementation decisions when requirements or system boundaries are incomplete.
* You understand how query execution, indexing, transaction processing, and durable state shape what developers and operators observe.
* You understand how concurrency control, isolation, replication, and snapshots shape consistency, durability, and recovery. You can apply those concepts when operations arrive out of order, components fail independently, or the network partitions.
* You write and debug concurrent production software in Rust, Go, C++, or another systems language. You can trace failures across process, network, and durable-state boundaries.
* You have operated stateful systems through rollouts, scaling events, incidents, and recovery. You know the difference between transient unavailability and incomplete or incorrect recovery, and when a system is safe to return to service.
* You have led investigations where failures crossed systems owned by several teams.

### **Bonus Points**

* You've worked on the internals of PostgreSQL, MySQL, Amazon Aurora, or another relational database and can trace a SQL operation from planning through commit.
* Your work on transaction processing or concurrency control has included defining snapshot visibility and recovery behavior.
* You've profiled database workloads and traced performance bottlenecks from query execution through durable storage.
* You've used deterministic simulation or another systematic method to uncover distributed-systems bugs that conventional tests missed.

new_jobs.title: Software Engineering Manager, AI Kernels & Performance Optimization — MTIA Software
new_jobs.description:
Meta designs and deploys its own AI systems. MTIA — the Meta Training and Inference Accelerator — is Meta's family of in-house AI accelerator ASICs, running recommendation and ranking workloads in production across Meta's data centers today and expanding into generative AI inference and training as successive silicon generations land.The MTIA Software team is part of the AI & Compute Foundation (ACF) organization within Meta Infrastructure. We build the entire stack a chip vendor would normally supply — compiler and LLVM toolchain, runtime, kernel authoring frameworks and libraries, developer tooling, and deep PyTorch integration — co-designing it with the silicon teams generation over generation.Within that stack, the AI Kernels and Performance Optimization team (KORE) owns the layer where silicon architecture meets arithmetic. Our mission is roofline-level performance and programmability at scale: we design and implement high-performance compute and communication kernels (GEMM, attention variants, normalization, collectives, elementwise and reduction fusions, sparse and quantized paths) against novel architectural features including matrix engines, on-chip reduction fabrics, and software-managed memory hierarchies. We ship kernel libraries with broad PyTorch operator coverage, build C++ and Python kernel authoring frameworks and DSL surfaces, and write production kernels against new architectures long before first silicon — turning hardware proposals into measured roofline evidence while the design can still change.We are seeking a Software Engineering Manager to lead a team of kernel and performance engineers doing this work. You will own the performance of workloads that serve billions of people, drive technical strategy for kernel development and optimization, and build a team that can deliver roofline-level performance on MTIA accelerators. Your team will profile and root-cause performance across the full stack — instruction scheduling, memory hierarchy and DMA behavior, on-chip interconnect, multi-device collectives — and drive fixes to the right layer, whether that is the kernel, compiler, runtime, or hardware. You will partner closely with silicon architecture teams on hardware/software co-design, quantifying the value of proposed features with real kernels and advocating for the changes the software stack needs. This is a hands-on technical leadership role where you will contribute directly to architectural decisions while enabling your team to move with speed and clarity.  
  
  

### **Software Engineering Manager, AI Kernels & Performance Optimization — MTIA Software Responsibilities:**

* Lead and manage a team of systems engineers delivering on multiple concurrent projects across ambiguous, high-impact areas of Meta's platform infrastructure

* Communicate team goals, technical decisions, and progress clearly to cross-functional partners and leadership, including written design proposals and postmortems
* Participate in org-wide engineering contributions, sharing effective workflows, tooling practices, and systems engineering patterns across the broader organization

  
  
  

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* 4+ years of experience in software engineering with a focus on systems-level software, platform infrastructure, or distributed systems
* 2+ years of experience managing or leading engineering teams, including setting technical direction and supporting engineer growth
* Experience driving technical roadmaps and executing against them with measurable outcomes in ambiguous or high-complexity environments
* Experience identifying and resolving engineering efficiency issues such as on-call burden, technical debt, or gaps in automation
* Experience collaborating across product, design, and data functions to deliver software that achieves business and user impact

  
  
  

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Track record of hands-on technical contribution as a manager, including authoring design documents, reviewing system architectures, or writing production code
* Experience with hardware/software co-design cycles: collaborating with silicon architects, validating architectural features with real kernels, and influencing hardware roadmaps based on software performance analysis
* Experience working on customized AI accelerators (TPU, AI ASICs, or similar non-GPU architectures) with direct involvement in kernel development and roofline enablement
* Familiarity with transformer and attention kernel design: FlashAttention-class algorithms, KV-cache management, paged and chunked attention, MoE routing and expert dispatch

George Mason University, a Carnegie Research I institution, is Virginia’s largest and most diverse university with more than 38,000 students. Located in Fairfax, Virginia, Mason is part of the Washington DC metropolitan area offering easy access to the scientific and political resources of the nation’s capital.
  
  
George Mason University is committed to advancing inclusion, access, and equal opportunity throughout our community. We believe that a broad range of voices, cultures, and perspectives brings vibrancy, innovation, and growth to an academic community.
  
  
The Landolt Mission team is responsible for developing and executing a NASA space-based mission through coordinated work across science, payload, spacecraft bus, software, systems engineering, integration and test, mission assurance, and project management functions. The unit provides an interdisciplinary research and training environment for faculty, postdoctoral researchers, engineers, staff, and students working collaboratively with federal, academic, commercial, and other external partners.
  
  
The Landolt Mission team supports mission formulation, systems engineering, subsystem coordination, technical trade studies, requirements development, verification and validation planning, assembly, integration and testing, technical documentation, mission reviews, and mission operations planning. The unit works collaboratively across payload, spacecraft bus, software, ground systems, mission operations, science, and programmatic interfaces to advance mission objectives and meet NASA requirements.
  
  
Statement on Building an Inclusive Culture: George Mason University's College of Science (Mason Science) is committed to advancing inclusive excellence and fostering an environment free from discrimination, harassment, and retaliation throughout our STEM community. At Mason Science, our values include cultivating an organizational culture that promotes belonging, respect, and civility. We believe that varied opinions, cultures, and perspectives are what provides vibrancy, innovation, and growth to an academic community. By prioritizing cultural responsiveness in academics, teaching, research, and global engagement, we strive to attract faculty and staff who exemplify the Mason Science mission and vision.

**About the Position:**

The Instrument Systems Engineer is sponsored by the NASA Landolt mission. The duties include (at a different level of involvement and responsibility):

* Contributes to all aspects of payload instrument design and development including mechanical, electrical, software, procedural, and regulatory compliance as a member of the instrument team.
* Participates in the assembly, integration, and testing of components, modules, and fully integrated instruments, ensuring seamless integration with the satellite bus.
* Runs data collection, analysis, and simulation studies to define the instrument performance. Develops procedures and techniques to process data from the space-based Landolt Mission instrument, while continuously enhancing its performance.

* Collaborates effectively within a diverse, multi-institutional team environment comprising scientists, engineers, students, project managers, and support staff across federal, academic, and commercial partners.
* Fosters a culture of engagement, diversity, inclusiveness, excellence, and innovation. Champions George Mason University's commitment to Access, Justice, Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion to create an inclusive and welcoming environment that promotes a commitment to safety, integrity, and teamwork.

**Responsibilities:**

Executes NASA Landolt Mission throughout its Lifecycle:

* Work closely with mission leadership; and

new_jobs.title: Software Engineering Manager, AI Kernels & Performance Optimization — MTIA Software
new_jobs.description:
Meta designs and deploys its own AI systems. MTIA — the Meta Training and Inference Accelerator — is Meta's family of in-house AI accelerator ASICs, running recommendation and ranking workloads in production across Meta's data centers today and expanding into generative AI inference and training as successive silicon generations land.The MTIA Software team is part of the AI & Compute Foundation (ACF) organization within Meta Infrastructure. We build the entire stack a chip vendor would normally supply — compiler and LLVM toolchain, runtime, kernel authoring frameworks and libraries, developer tooling, and deep PyTorch integration — co-designing it with the silicon teams generation over generation.Within that stack, the AI Kernels and Performance Optimization team (KORE) owns the layer where silicon architecture meets arithmetic. Our mission is roofline-level performance and programmability at scale: we design and implement high-performance compute and communication kernels (GEMM, attention variants, normalization, collectives, elementwise and reduction fusions, sparse and quantized paths) against novel architectural features including matrix engines, on-chip reduction fabrics, and software-managed memory hierarchies. We ship kernel libraries with broad PyTorch operator coverage, build C++ and Python kernel authoring frameworks and DSL surfaces, and write production kernels against new architectures long before first silicon — turning hardware proposals into measured roofline evidence while the design can still change.We are seeking a Software Engineering Manager to lead a team of kernel and performance engineers doing this work. You will own the performance of workloads that serve billions of people, drive technical strategy for kernel development and optimization, and build a team that can deliver roofline-level performance on MTIA accelerators. Your team will profile and root-cause performance across the full stack — instruction scheduling, memory hierarchy and DMA behavior, on-chip interconnect, multi-device collectives — and drive fixes to the right layer, whether that is the kernel, compiler, runtime, or hardware. You will partner closely with silicon architecture teams on hardware/software co-design, quantifying the value of proposed features with real kernels and advocating for the changes the software stack needs. This is a hands-on technical leadership role where you will contribute directly to architectural decisions while enabling your team to move with speed and clarity.  
  
  

### **Software Engineering Manager, AI Kernels & Performance Optimization — MTIA Software Responsibilities:**

* Lead and manage a team of systems engineers delivering on multiple concurrent projects across ambiguous, high-impact areas of Meta's platform infrastructure

**Overview**

Come build community, explore your passions, and do your best work.

The Windows Servicing and Delivery (WSD) organization is responsible for delivering protected, productive, and predictable servicing experiences for Windows customers around the world. As security threats evolve and engineering systems grow in scale and complexity, WSD is investing in intelligent automation, large-scale quality analytics, and AI-powered validation platforms that improve the speed, quality, transparency, and reliability of the monthly security fixes delivered across the Windows ecosystem.

The Validation team plays a critical role in validating Windows servicing releases, including the monthly security fixes shipped to customers. The team develops and operates modern validation platforms, automation frameworks, telemetry systems, and AI-powered engineering solutions that help identify regressions, quantify release quality, and reduce deployment risk across consumer, enterprise, cloud, and original equipment manufacturer (OEM) environments.

Our mission is to help engineering teams make better release decisions faster through trusted validation signals, actionable insights, scalable automation, durable platform services, and responsible use of AI technologies. By transforming validation from a collection of isolated tests into an intelligent engineering platform, we help ensure that monthly Windows security releases meet rigorous standards for reliability, security, and customer quality.

As a **Software Engineer** on the Validation team, you will contribute to software, services, automation systems, and AI-enabled solutions that improve validation effectiveness, engineering productivity, and the quality of monthly Windows security releases.

You will work with experienced engineers, validation specialists, and cross-functional partners to design, implement, test, deploy, and maintain cloud services, automation frameworks, telemetry pipelines, quality analytics platforms, and agent-based engineering experiences used to assess release readiness and security-fix quality.

In this role, you will help modernize how the quality of Windows security fixes is validated and measured at scale. Your contributions will improve validation efficiency, strengthen confidence in monthly security releases, accelerate issue detection, and help deliver secure, reliable, and high-quality Windows updates to customers around the world.
